J-lens assessment: example/tiny-model

2 candidate lenses compared with a reference lens and a plain baseline, on 2 texts, in 4 comparisons.

  1. Summary
  2. Identity
  3. Text 1: heldout/essays.jsonl
  4. Text 2: heldout/recipes.jsonl
  5. Lenses
  6. Limits

Summary

A J-lens translates a model’s internal state at one layer into the tokens (word pieces) the model is leaning toward. This report asks how well each candidate lens reads the model’s own final prediction, layer by layer, next to a reference lens and next to reading the layer with no lens at all.

What was compared

  • Model example/tiny-model at revision abababababababababababababababababababab.
  • Reference lens: lens-round-1.
  • Candidate lenses (2): lens-round-2, lens-mixed.
  • Texts (2): heldout/essays.jsonl (2 of 2 rows assessed), heldout/recipes.jsonl (1 of 2 rows assessed; 1 skipped).
  • Plain baseline: each layer read directly, with no lens, at the same token positions.

Result, text by text

“More closely” below means a higher top-k overlap with the model’s final prediction, the main measure here. Both measures are explained at the end of this summary.

On heldout/essays.jsonl

  • Candidate lens-round-2 matched the model’s final prediction more closely than the reference at 2 of 3 layers (0, 2), less closely at no layer, and equally at 1 of 3 layers (1). It matched more closely than the plain baseline at all 3 layers.
  • Candidate lens-mixed matched the model’s final prediction more closely than the reference at 1 of 3 layers (1), less closely at 2 of 3 layers (0, 2). It matched more closely than the plain baseline at 2 of 3 layers (0–1).

Closest reading at each layer, by top-k overlap: candidate lens-round-2 at 2 layers (0, 2); candidate lens-mixed at 1 layer (1).

On heldout/recipes.jsonl

  • Candidate lens-round-2 matched the model’s final prediction more closely than the reference at 2 of 3 layers (0–1), less closely at no layer, and equally at 1 of 3 layers (2). It matched more closely than the plain baseline at 2 of 3 layers (0–1).
  • Candidate lens-mixed matched the model’s final prediction more closely than the reference at all 3 layers, less closely at no layer. It matched more closely than the plain baseline at all 3 layers. This text is not held out for this pair of lenses.

Closest reading at each layer, by top-k overlap: candidate lens-mixed at 3 layers (0–2).

Each count is the number of layers where the candidate’s stored value is the closer one, out of the layers where both values are stored.

Read with care: These are layer-by-layer comparisons of stored values. The engine computed no average across layers, no interval, and no significance test, so this page shows none. A small difference at one layer may not be a meaningful one.

This assessment does not qualify a lens. Whether a lens is good enough for a study remains the researcher’s decision.

How to read the numbers

Top-k overlap is the main measure. Take the k tokens the model finally ranks highest at a position, and the k tokens a reading ranks highest at the same position. The overlap is the share they have in common, from 0 (none) to 1 (the same k tokens). Higher means the reading is closer to the final prediction. k is 5.

Jensen–Shannon divergence compares the two full sets of token probabilities, in nats. 0 means identical, and lower means closer. The engine averaged both measures over the assessed token positions of a text.

Every comparison uses the one reference lens named above. The comparison SHA-256 is the engine’s digest of that entry. This page recomputes it only to check that the entry is unchanged.

Baseline

The plain baseline, also called the logit lens: the layer’s own state is read through the model’s final normalization and output layer with no lens applied, at the same token positions as the lenses. It is stored for every layer of every comparison.

Limits

What these measures show

Top-k overlap and Jensen–Shannon divergence say how closely a reading at one layer matches the model’s own final prediction, on the token positions that were assessed. They do not show that a lens is causally faithful, that it will read other kinds of text as well, or that a difference between two lenses is larger than chance. A close match on these texts is a reason to look further, not a qualification.

Recorded by the engine: how values were averaged
Equal weight per assessed token position; first eligible positions up to the displayed cap.
Recorded by the engine: limitations
Distributional agreement measures readout stability and agreement with the final residual at these positions. It does not prove causal validity, dataset independence, or adequacy for every research question.
Recorded by the engine: qualification
notPerformed
